successors.note: Buganda 'became the centre of the Protectorate of Uganda'; the kingdom kept its Kabaka and Lukiiko under the Uganda Agreement of 1900 and was disestablished in 1967 (Buganda page), so the British tint is the continuation of the kingdom, not its disappearance.

capitals.name: Mengo (Kampala)
capitals.note: The infobox gives Mengo and the body Lubaga as the capital; the page dates no capital and Kasubi appears only as a burial site. The seat moved with each kabaka; Mengo is the nineteenth-century one.

correction.text: the first state of Kyadondo, Busiro and Mawokota (Wakiso, Mpigi and Kampala districts)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1300-1799: the first state, 'covering Kyadondo, Busiro, and Mawokota'. The page puts Kintu's unification 'around the 13th century' and the foundation between the 12th and 14th centuries; 'In the 16th century, Bunyoro invaded Buganda, killing Kabaka Nakinge', so the core was small and at times beaten. No area is given for this period.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1800-1893: Buganda after the capture of Buddu, with its later expansion (the Buganda page: 'during the reigns of Kimbugwe, Katerega, and Mutebi during the 17th and 18th centuries', canoe fleets 'from the 1840s', Ukerewe in 1878, raids on Busoga and the Buvuma Islands in 1879). The shape is the gazetteer's Buganda region (a 100 km disk round Kampala, 111 cells) plus Buddu (the Buddu page: 'Bukomansimbi, Lwengo, Kalungu, Masaka and Kyotera'; Kyotera is a new district without an admin-1 polygon and lies in the gazetteer's Rakai polygon, so it is drawn with Kooki), minus the 12 cells (about 3,000 km2) of Mubende, Nakasongola and Kiboga that kingdom-of-bunyoro's 1590-1829 keyframe also holds: no page dates their passing to Buganda (the Bunyoro page has only the 1964 referendum that returned the lost counties of Buyaga and Bugangaizi), so they stay with Bunyoro. Kooki is not in the shape: the Buganda page says 'Kooki was made a tributary', so it is a vassal tint (ledger 3 and 4). Result 113 cells, 28,578 km2; with Kooki (Rakai, 4,046 km2) about 32,600 km2. The infobox gives 61,403.2 km2 for the kingdom with no year (the page does not say whether lake water is included): ratio 0.47, 0.53 with Kooki; Cliopatria has no Buganda row, so there is no second figure. Busoga: the Buganda page says 'parts of Busoga' were conquered, the Busoga page that 'the Baganda were unable to conquer Busoga' and held only chiefs on the south shore; the disk takes in 9 cells of Jinja, Kamuli and Luuka districts, undated. [Repair af-05, 2026-10-19: Buddu and the Bunyoro cut added; Kooki moved out of the shape into a vassal tint.]

region.text: the first state of Kyadondo, Busiro and Mawokota (Wakiso, Mpigi and Kampala districts)

ledger.note: c. 1300: Kato Kintu founds Buganda in Busiro. 'unification around the 13th century by the first king, Kato Kintu'; infobox 'Founded by Kato Kintu: 12th/13th/14th century'; 'Likely founded between the 12th and 14th centuries, with the first state covering Kyadondo, Busiro, and Mawokota'. The year 1300 is a placeholder for the century; Kintu's conquests 'are estimated to have occurred sometime between 1200 and 1400 AD'. [Repair af-05, 2026-10-19: the Kato Kintu page has 'Kato Kintu Kakulukuku (fl. Late 13th century)' and 'Reign: late 13th century' in the infobox but 'King of Buganda early fourteenth century' in its succession table, and no year for the founding of Buganda; the Buganda page's 'around the 13th century' and 'between 1200 and 1400 AD' agree, so 1300 stays a placeholder at confidence 1.]

region.text: Buddu, the Bunyoro province captured by Buganda (Masaka, Lwengo, Bukomansimbi and Kalungu districts)

ledger.note: Late 18th century: Buganda captures Buddu from Bunyoro. Buddu page: Kabaka Jjunju (r. 1780-1797) 'defeated the Nyoro army and captured Buddu, which had been a province of Bunyoro' (no year; the Buganda page has 'Junju (c.1790-1800)'); the Bunyoro page: 'Buganda seized the Kooki and Buddu regions from Bunyoro at the end of the century'; the Kooki page: 'annexing the province of Buddu in the late 1700s'. 1800 is a placeholder inside 1780-1800, kept to match kingdom-of-bunyoro's 1800 loss. Buddu is drawn as Masaka, Lwengo, Bukomansimbi and Kalungu; the Buddu page also counts Kyotera, which lies in the Rakai polygon drawn as Kooki. [Repair af-05, 2026-10-19: Kooki split off into a vassal_start (ledger 3).]

region.text: the rest of the Buganda region beyond the first state and Buddu: the counties added under Kimbugwe, Katerega and Mutebi in the 17th and 18th centuries

ledger.note: 17th-18th centuries (1800 is a placeholder): Buganda grows from the first state of Kyadondo, Busiro and Mawokota (17 cells) to the whole Buganda region (80 more cells besides Buddu). Buganda page: 'Buganda grew to become one of the largest and most powerful states in East Africa during the 18th and the 19th centuries'; the expansion 'occurred during the reigns of Kimbugwe, Katerega, and Mutebi during the 17th and 18th centuries'; 'Among those conquered was Buddu, parts of Busoga, and parts of the Karagwe'. No page dates a county or names whose land it was, so the counterpart is 'nobody'; the Busoga page says instead that 'the Baganda were unable to conquer Busoga' and had influence only on the south shore. Mubende, Nakasongola and Kiboga stay with Bunyoro. [Repair af-05, 2026-10-19: added to explain the jump from 17 to 113 cells.]

region.text: the Kooki kingdom (Rakai district; Kyotera, a Buddu county, lies in the same polygon)

ledger.note: Late 18th century: Kooki becomes a tributary of Buganda. Kooki page: after annexing Buddu 'in the late 1700s' Buganda 'established a tributary relationship with the Kooki Kingdom in order to gain access to the large market in Karagwe'; the Buganda page: 'Kooki was made a tributary'. Kooki broke away from Bunyoro-Kitara c. 1740 (Kooki page infobox), so it was not Bunyoro's to lose in 1800, unlike the Bunyoro page's 'seized the Kooki and Buddu regions'. 1800 is a placeholder. [Repair af-05, 2026-10-19: replaces the annexation of Rakai in the 1800 gain.]

region.text: Mwanga's 'land and tributary states', placed under IBEAC protection

ledger.note: 1891: Mwanga places Buganda under the company. Uganda Protectorate page: 'Mwanga concluded a treaty with Lugard whereby Mwanga would place his land and tributary states under the protection of the IBEAC' (1891; the History of Buganda page has 1892). [Reviewer af-05, 2026-10-19: added as the mirror of the imperial-british-east-africa-company event.]

region.text: Mwanga's 'land and tributary states', placed under IBEAC protection

ledger.note: 31 March 1893: 'the IBEAC formally ended its involvement in Uganda' (Uganda Protectorate page); British protection follows on 18 June 1894. [Reviewer af-05, 2026-10-19: added as the mirror of the imperial-british-east-africa-company event.]

region.text: the Kooki kingdom (Rakai district; Kyotera, a Buddu county, lies in the same polygon)

ledger.note: June 1894: the tributary relation ends with the kingdom (placeholder; the Kooki page does not date the end of the tribute). Kooki page: in 1893 rebels fled 'into the independent kingdom of Kooki'; Ndahura II went to Kampala in 1894; Kooki signed an allegiance agreement before the British commissioner in 1896 (ratified 4 May 1903) and was 'Incorporated into Buganda: 18 November 1896' (infobox), a year after this dossier ends. [Repair af-05, 2026-10-19.]

ledger.note: 18 June 1894: Uganda becomes a British protectorate. 'On 18 June 1894, the British government declared that Uganda would come under British protection as a Protectorate'; Mwanga had placed his land and tributary states under the Imperial British East Africa Company in 1891 (the History of Buganda page has the treaty with Lugard in 1892), the company ended its involvement on 31 March 1893. The kingdom continues under the Uganda Agreement of 1900.

wars.name: Battle of Rwangabi
wars.outcome: Bunyoro victory: its army 'achieved a significant victory against the Baganda' in February 1886 in the armed struggle over the ivory trade; no border moved.

wars.name: Buganda religious wars and the Lugard intervention
wars.outcome: Mwanga II was ousted in a Muslim coup in 1888; Lugard came for the Imperial British East Africa Company in 1890; Mwanga signed a treaty in 1891; in 1892 'the Protestants and Catholics resumed their struggle for supremacy'. The company handed over to the British government in 1893.
wars.note: Faction fighting inside Buganda; the pages record no territory changing hands.

certainty.note: Kingdom frontiers are approximate throughout: counties named by the page, no survey or treaty line before the colonial period.

sources.title: Buganda
sources.note: Founding between the 12th and 14th centuries, the first state of Kyadondo, Busiro and Mawokota; Mutesa and Mwanga; infobox area 61,403 km2 (modern kingdom).

sources.title: History of Buganda
sources.note: 1840s expansion by war canoe, 1862, 1884 Mwanga II, 1892 Lugard treaty; thin on territory.

sources.title: Uganda Protectorate
sources.note: 1888 coup, 1890 Lugard for the IBEAC, 1891 Mwanga's treaty, 31 March 1893 IBEAC ends, 18 June 1894 protectorate, 1900 Uganda Agreement, 1900 Toro treaty, 1901 Ankole treaty, 1902 transfer to Kenya.

sources.title: Bunyoro
sources.note: Founded late 16th century by Rukidi-Mpuga; 80,000 km2 at its 17th-century peak; Kooki and Buddu lost to Buganda; Tooro separates in the 1830s; Rwangabi 1886; Kabalega captured and Bunyoro annexed 1899; 1964 referendum.

sources.title: Buddu
sources.note: County of Buganda; 'Bukomansimbi, Lwengo, Kalungu, Masaka and Kyotera'; Kabaka Jjunju (r. 1780-1797) captured it from Bunyoro; no year.

sources.title: Kooki
sources.note: Kingdom in Rakai district c. 1740-1896; broke away from Bunyoro c. 1740; tributary of Buganda after Buddu; 1896 agreement; incorporated into Buganda 18 November 1896.

sources.title: Busoga
sources.note: 'The Baganda were unable to conquer Busoga'; Kabaka's influence in south Busoga only; no central ruler before 1906; 10,318 km2.

notes:
New state (Cliopatria has no Buganda row). Four pages: Buganda, History of Buganda, Uganda Protectorate and Bunyoro. The Buganda pages are thin on dated territory: no year for Kintu, none for the reigns of Kimera to Suna, none for the annexation of Busoga and only a reign (Jjunju, 1780-1797 on the Buddu page) for Buddu, and nothing on the lost counties of Buyaga and Bugangaizi (Bunyoro page: regained by Bunyoro after a 1964 referendum), the 1890 Anglo-German treaty or the 1900 Uganda Agreement's counties and month. Those are left out, not filled from memory.

Dates that disagree: Mwanga's treaty with Lugard 1891 (Uganda Protectorate page) or 1892 (History of Buganda page); the Buganda page puts the protectorate in 1884 in the body and 1894 in the infobox; independence 8 October 1960 or 9 October 1962; the restoration 24 July or 31 July 1993. The founding year 1300 and the 1800 gain are placeholders at confidence 1.

The Bunyoro page also records an agreement of July 1890 'whereby the entire Buganda region north of Lake Victoria was given to' Great Britain (a great-power spheres line; no change of rule).

Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-bunyoro (this batch), british-colonial-empire (eu-11: the Uganda Protectorate of 1894 with Buganda as a protected kingdom), Busoga (Busoga chiefdoms, no dossier), Ukerewe (Mutesa's fleet of 1878). Gazetteer names needed: Kyadondo, Busiro, Mawokota (counties), Buddu, Kooki, Busoga.

Repair pass, 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): (1) the 1800 keyframe was the bare 100 km disk of the gazetteer's Buganda region, which holds none of Buddu or Kooki; it is now the region plus Masaka, Lwengo, Bukomansimbi and Kalungu (Buddu), minus Mubende, Nakasongola and Kiboga (12 cells that kingdom-of-bunyoro's 1590-1829 shape also holds; the cut leaves them with Bunyoro until a page dates their passing, and the 22 further cells that Bunyoro's 1830 keyframe drops with no event are Bunyoro's open question). (2) Kooki is a tributary (Buganda page: 'Kooki was made a tributary'), so it is a vassal tint from 1800 to 1894, counterpart 'Kooki', not annexed land; the Kooki page puts the kingdom's break from Bunyoro at c. 1740, so Bunyoro's 1800 loss of Rakai in its own dossier is doubtful. (3) A gain of 80 cells (counterpart nobody, confidence 1) now explains the jump from the first state to the whole region. (4) The Kato Kintu page gives no year for the founding (late 13th or early 14th century), so 1300 stays a placeholder. Not settled: the Busoga cells of the shape (Buganda page 'parts of Busoga' against the Busoga page 'unable to conquer'), the date of Buddu inside 1780-1800, when the tribute of Kooki stopped, and the Kooki incorporation of 18 November 1896 (after this dossier ends). Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-kooki (c. 1740-1896). Gazetteer names needed: Kyotera (district, Buddu county; split from Rakai).
